dropped.claim: IDACORP operates a stable regulated utility with improving earnings—net income rose from $261.2M in 2023 to $323.5M in 2025, marking an 18th consecutive year of growth—yet the investment case depends critically on execution of a $6.3B–$7.2B five-year capital program where operating cash flow of $601.8M covers only half of 2025 capex of $1.2B, producing -$577.5M free cash flow and requiring sustained access to capital (long-term debt grew from $2.8B in 2023 to $3.3B in 2025; shares increased 4.2% in 2025) while navigating competing risks: residential usage per customer declined from 1,032 kWh in 2012 to 922 kWh in 2025 despite an FCA mechanism designed to mitigate this, industrial load forecasts remain unproven (risk of stranded costs if new customers miss ramp rates), and regulatory lag persists despite multiple rate cases (2023, 2024, 2025) and the December 2025 Settlement Stipulation, creating uncertainty over whether the substantial rate base growth translates to timely and adequate returns.

IDACORP demonstrates stable regulated utility fundamentals—18 consecutive years of net income growth, robust customer growth of 2.3% in 2025, record retail sales, and regulatory mechanisms (FCA, power cost adjustment) that mitigate volume and cost risks—but the sheer scale of the $6.3B–$7.2B capital program relative to $601.8M operating cash flow creates execution risk and dependence on external financing (debt up from $2.8B to $3.3B in two years, shares up 4.2% in 2025) while key uncertainties remain unresolved: the approved ROE and rate base treatment in the 2025 Settlement Stipulation, the realization of industrial load forecasts that underpin the buildout, and the pace of regulatory recovery for major projects. The bull case—that regulatory mechanisms work and rate base growth drives earnings—is credible given the 18-year track record, but the bear case—that capital intensity outstrips cash generation and industrial load proves optimistic—warrants monitoring before deeper commitment. A 'Watch' stance allows time to assess 2026 rate case outcomes, industrial customer ramp progress, and financing execution.
